# Coupled pilot

Run the pilot using `scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py`.

## Case Selection

By default, without any `--case` flags, all cases defined in the suite run (the no-filter default).

You can selectively run specific cases by passing one or more `--case` flags:

```bash
python3 scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py --case alpha --case gamma
```

### Behavior Details

- **Original Suite Order**: Regardless of the order in which `--case` flags are specified on the command line (e.g., `--case gamma --case alpha`), selected cases are always executed and recorded in their original suite order.
- **Duplicates**: If a case ID is specified multiple times (e.g., `--case alpha --case gamma --case alpha`), duplicates are ignored so that each named case runs exactly once.
- **Unknown IDs**: If any unknown case ID is provided via `--case`, execution fails immediately with an error before creating output directories or executing any cases.

arguments.content:
# Coupled pilot

Run the pilot using scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py.

## Case Selection

Use the `--case` flag to select specific cases to run. You can specify this flag multiple times to select multiple cases.

Example:
```
python scripts/run_coupled_pilot.py --case alpha --case gamma
```

This will run only the cases with IDs `alpha` and `gamma` in the original suite order.

### Important Notes

- Duplicate case IDs specified with repeated `--case` flags are ignored; each case runs only once.
- Cases are always run in the original suite order, regardless of the order of `--case` flags.
- If no `--case` flag is provided, all cases run by default.
- If any unknown case IDs are specified, the pilot will fail immediately with an error before producing output or running any cases.
- The pilot preserves existing output directories and will not overwrite existing results.
- Independent oracles run as usual regardless of case selection.
